topics.flagship-ru-ua: Ukrainian authorities say a Russian drone struck emergency workers on rescue missions in southern Ukraine on Sunday, hitting a former school and nearby shelter that Russian guided bombs had earlier hit while residents waited for humanitarian aid (3 outlets). Russian strikes on energy infrastructure reportedly left more than 600,000 people without power, and the Russian-run management of the Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant says it has lost its external power supply. Single-outlet reports also cite Russian claims of hitting two power substations and three ships in the Black Sea, strikes near Kyiv ahead of talks in Abu Dhabi, and drone attacks that reportedly killed 50 people in one Zaporizhzhia attack.
topics.flagship-ir-il: An airstrike on homes in a village near Sanaa, Yemen, killed at least 25 people and wounded 30, mostly women and children, according to the Houthi-run Health Ministry (4 outlets); the input does not say who carried it out. Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot says he will seek a wide government after a deadlocked election, though his path to power is uncertain. Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it has lifted its self-imposed limit on ballistic missile range, and Iranian media suggested explosions in southern Iran were not US strikes even as both sides reported ships hit. A single outlet reports a Houthi missile damaged the Aramco tower in Riyadh.
topics.T15: Coverage is sparse and minor: a single-outlet story describes Florida flood survivors sheltering with retired first responders because hotels were full or too costly. Another covers a military medicine disaster-response working group co-chaired by Indonesia and the US.
topics.T01: Stories filed under this topic are generic or tangential. They include a EU Parliament flag-lowering after the Krakow shooting, Secretary of State Rubio's planned attendance at a G7 foreign ministers meeting in France after Republican midterm losses, and an analysis of China's food-import dependence as a possible constraint on a Taiwan war. The Yemen airstrike and the European hoax bomb threats are cross-referenced.
topics.T02: Heavy rain is worsening humanitarian conditions in Gaza, where most homes are damaged or destroyed (3 outlets). Single-outlet reports cover displaced Naga communities in Manipur seeking recognition and aid, hunger in Somalia amid reduced US assistance, child malnutrition in Sudan, and drug-resistant infections among wounded Ukrainian soldiers. Nigeria's displaced population of 3.6 million also draws a mention.
topics.T03: The only item is a single-outlet report that Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson reminded Germany of its alleged role in chemical attacks during the Iran-Iraq War. It describes no new chemical or biological incident.
topics.T04: Coverage is sparse and generic. A UK survey found fewer than a third of vets believe the profession is ready for a major animal disease outbreak, a Texas county medical reserve corps is recruiting volunteers, and one piece discusses climate change and emerging disease risk. No active outbreak is reported.
topics.T05: Pedro Alliana became president of Paraguay after predecessor Santiago Pena was impeached over a banking crisis that left almost half the country unable to access accounts (3 outlets); the headline also says Pena was arrested. Single-outlet reports discuss speculation about Pete Hegseth's standing after Susie Wiles' exit as White House chief of staff, and a Japan-China rift one year after Takaichi's Taiwan remarks.
topics.T06: Iranian authorities executed three men on Sunday for allegedly acting on behalf of Israel and the US during January anti-government protests (6 outlets). France is seeing renewed nationwide cost-of-living protests, with about 70,000 security personnel deployed in Paris despite bans on gatherings (2 outlets). Single-outlet reports say Macron's approval has fallen to 13 percent and that he reportedly has a secret bunker outside Paris.
topics.T07: There are no standalone stories; the only entry is a cross-reference to a Middle East item headlined 'Israel threatens Iran yet again', with no details provided.
topics.T08: A 24-year-old man with far-right views drove into a central Krakow square and opened fire, killing six and wounding 15 before police shot him; Poland began two days of national mourning and prosecutors opened a terrorism investigation (11 outlets). Single-outlet reports say more than 50 people were killed in a militant attack on Daleti in western Ethiopia, a policeman was killed in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and AFRICOM announced its 91st Somalia strike of the year.
topics.T10: Coverage is minor and single-sourced: the Russian Mi-28NM has reportedly fired a cruise missile in Ukraine, as Russia, the US and India develop longer-range attack helicopters. Indian artillery-shell exports to Europe are reportedly at a record, and US defense contractors may face more scrutiny under the new Congress in 2027.
topics.T11: The IDF announced a military exercise in the Galilee and near Be'er Sheva from Monday to Wednesday evening, with increased movement of security forces and vehicles. It says there is no security threat.
topics.T12: Dozens of flights across Europe were targeted by hoax bomb threats this week, causing diversions and emergency landings (2 outlets). Italy's Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers for leaking Foreign Minister Tajani's personal data on the dark web (2 outlets). US federal agencies warned on Nov. 5 of ongoing hacking of industrial refrigeration systems, following attacks on European retailers.
topics.T13: Coverage is thin: the UN says it will expand cooperation with Afghanistan as more than 8 million migrants have returned home, and Canada has reportedly announced plans for 2.3 million additional migrants. The rest is documentary or opinion content.
topics.T16: The main theme is the aftermath of the US midterms, in which Democrats won both houses of Congress; Republicans including DeSantis and Cruz reacted harshly, and Trump's hold on the party is being questioned (2 outlets). Single-outlet reports cover disputed Israeli claims of foreign election interference used against a possible Eisenkot-led government, South Africa's ANC posting its worst results ever, and early 2028 and 2027 campaign positioning in the US and Nigeria.

bluf: Poland began two days of national mourning after a 24-year-old man with far-right views drove into a central Krakow square and opened fire, killing six and wounding 15 before police shot him; prosecutors have opened a terrorism investigation (11 outlets). Ukraine says a Russian drone struck emergency workers in southern Ukraine on Sunday, hitting a former school and shelter that Russian guided bombs had earlier hit (3 outlets). The Houthi-run Health Ministry says an airstrike on homes near Sanaa killed at least 25 people and wounded 30, mostly women and children; the input does not identify the attacker. In Israel, Gadi Eisenkot says he will try to form a wide government after a deadlocked election, but his path to power is uncertain. The Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant has lost its external power supply, according to its Russian-installed management, while strikes on energy infrastructure reportedly left more than 600,000 Ukrainians without power. Separately, Iran's Revolutionary Guard says it has lifted its self-imposed limit on ballistic missile range (3 outlets), a reported shift in posture. In Paraguay, Pedro Alliana became president after Santiago Pena was impeached over a banking crisis that left almost half the country unable to access accounts (3 outlets).
